title: Countries and devices
prompt: Before choosing which apps to test in which markets, the product team wants every combination of country and preferred device that members have. Write `solve(users)` so it returns each combination once, in a fixed order.
rules: Return two columns, `country` and `preferred_device`, with each combination exactly once.
Sort by `country` from A to Z, then by `preferred_device` from A to Z.
A missing value counts as its own value: a combination with a missing country or device appears once. Missing countries go after all others, and within a country a missing device goes last.
hints: Keep the two columns first, then remove repeated combinations with `distinct()`.
`distinct()` treats two missing values as the same, so they collapse into one row.
An ascending sort puts missing values first. Use `asc_nulls_last()` on both sort columns.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(users):
    # Return each country and device combination once, in order.
    return users
explanation: Select the two columns, then `distinct()`: `users.select("country", "preferred_device").distinct()`. The order matters: `distinct()` on the whole table compares every column, so two members with the same country and device but different ids are both kept. `distinct()` treats missing values as equal, so all members with no device in one country become one row. Then sort with missing values last on both keys: `orderBy(F.col("country").asc_nulls_last(), F.col("preferred_device").asc_nulls_last())`. A plain `orderBy("country", "preferred_device")` puts the missing ones first. `dropDuplicates(["country", "preferred_device"])` before the `select` gives the same combinations.
